TOOLING BURST T4e-r1 — SPEC § 7 row "T4e — peak decomposition" AS CORRECTED (Run C-5, E0-p step 2). task_id "T4e-r1". T4e-01 delivered a correct implementation of a WRONG row: its 7 pieces are band-layer unions (the contour as one disconnected piece, each grey plane as another). A burst made of those flies the outline away from its fill — a sticker explosion of layers. The corrected row (read it verbatim) wants SPATIAL SHARDS: tongues and core wedges, each carrying all its bands with the contour attached. Amend your own oracle/peak_pieces.py (keep isolate/quantise; replace decompose) and tests/test_peak_pieces.py accordingly.

Read ONLY, in this order:
1. /Users/admin/Games/reincarnated-collaboration/astra_test_01/burst/SPEC.md — § 0, § 1, and § 7 (the intro paragraph, the row "T4e — peak decomposition" — your contract; its Acceptance column is how your work is measured — and the row "T4h — piece-burst template" that CONSUMES your output; design pieces.json so T4h can read it without guessing).
2. /Users/admin/Games/reincarnated-collaboration/astra_test_01/burst/BURST_RULES.md (the TOOLING row).
3. export/vfx_material.gdshader (the value-index contract: source R carries band = round(R/255×3) ∈ {0,1,2,3}; alpha is independent coverage), export/effect_kit.py (kit schema; `distance_fields`), oracle/vfx_measure.py (coverage conventions), and the INPUT peak: runs/C-5/artifacts/E0p-peak-01/fire_peak_01_512.png — the WORKING asset (the painter delivered 1254²; the conductor resampled it to 512² with Lanczos ×0.408 so the body spans ≈ 306 px = 2.35 BH at 1:1; the raw original fire_peak_01.png is beside it for reference only) (painted by Astra as a four-plane greyscale body on either a transparent background or a flat #00ff00 plate — inspect it first and report which; the receipt runs/C-5/artifacts/E0p-peak-01/receipt.json says what the painter claimed).
Do not read anything else. No web. No agents. No image generation. No pip install. stdlib + Pillow + numpy + scipy ONLY.

BUILD exactly the corrected SPEC row — same CLI and file layout as T4e-01; decompose(index_map, alpha, centre=None) now: (a) body silhouette = alpha > 0 (as before); (b) centre = coverage centroid unless given; (c) find tongue tips = local maxima of distance-from-centre along the contour (prominence ≥ 0.15 × body radius), tongue roots = the contour concavities between tips (minima of distance-from-centre); (d) watershed on the negative distance transform of the silhouette, seeded at each tip and at 3–6 seeds spaced around the centre inside the core (core radius = the largest inscribed circle), with a boundary cost that follows contour concavities; (e) a tongue longer than 1.5 × core radius is split at its waist (narrowest width along its axis) into base + tip pieces; (f) merge slivers < 24 px into the neighbour sharing the longest border; guarantee every piece is ONE connected component (split any multi-component result into its components and re-merge components < 24 px); (g) per piece write piece_NNN.png = the index RGB (band × 85) + alpha of its own pixels on the full canvas (bbox recorded), pivot = coverage centroid (nearest mask pixel if outside), radial angle/distance, dominant_band, band_histogram, area, tip point; pieces.json + contact sheet as before (distinct colour per piece, numbered at pivots).
Tests (unittest, stdlib): a synthetic five-tongued body (a disc with five unequal lobes, two bands each) → 8–15 pieces, every piece one component, every piece ≥ 2 bands, union equal to the source coverage, largest piece ≤ 25 %; a pivot-outside-mask case (a crescent) resolved to the nearest mask pixel; a long tongue split at its waist; the keyed-plate path on a synthetic green-plate body with ≤ 1-px fringe.
ACCEPTANCE on the real peak (report exact numbers in runs/C-5/t3/T4e-r1/acceptance.json): ≥ 12 and ≤ 40 pieces; each ONE connected component; union == source coverage within ± 0.5 % of area; every pivot inside its own mask; no band-pure piece ≥ 200 px; largest piece ≤ 25 % of the body; RED: union ≠ source; a pivot outside its mask; a piece with two components; a band-pure piece ≥ 200 px. If the painter's output is NOT four clean planes (gradients, glow, > 4 levels), do not fix it by heavier quantisation — quantise as specified, report the band histogram and the fraction of pixels farther than 20 luminance levels from their nearest band, and mark the run DELIVERED_WITH_CONCERNS naming the defect (the conductor decides whether the peak is re-painted).
Then run the FULL suite: `cd /Users/admin/Games/reincarnated-collaboration/astra_test_01/burst && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -B tests/run_t0c.py` — expected: all green except the five standing reds (test_f04_outside_at_least_three; three test_named_genuine_annuli_retained subtests; test_synthetic_contract_and_grid); report tests_run, successful, and name every red.

DO NOT touch: lane/, bible/, fixtures/, briefs/, SPEC.md, BURST_RULES.md, REGISTER_CARD.md, JUDGE_RUBRIC.md, MANIFEST.sha256, receipt.schema.json, transcribe.schema.json, export/ (T4h owns the runtime side), any existing test file other than tests/test_peak_pieces.py (yours; rewrite freely), anything under runs/ except runs/C-5/t3/T4e-r1/ (write the pieces there: runs/C-5/t3/T4e-r1/pieces/; leave runs/C-5/t3/T4e/ untouched as the record of T4e-01). Do not run git. Temporary files ONLY under runs/C-5/t3/T4e-r1/ (set TMPDIR there; the runner's own reports under tests/ are expected — inventory them). Write out/files.json listing every file you added or changed with sha256.
RETURN: the receipt (task_id "T4e-r1"): files = every added/changed path with sha256; images = 0 (INTEGER); calls_used; status DELIVERED / DELIVERED_WITH_CONCERNS / FAILED with concerns listed honestly.
